c: Paper 1 is Computer Systems (sections 1.1–1.6); Paper 2 covers algorithms, programming, robustness, Boolean logic and languages (2.1–2.5). Each paper counts for half the GCSE.
Look at the command word and the actual mark scheme. Ask whether the problem was missing knowledge, an incomplete explanation, a tracing error or a calculation mistake.

Write a technical point, then link it to the effect in the situation. 'RAM is fast' is vague; 'RAM holds running instructions and working data so the CPU can access them quickly' is a stronger explanation.
Choose two named specification points. Test without notes, compare with the mark scheme, correct mistakes, then answer a different question a few days later.

m.title: Model a stronger exam answer
m.q: A learner answers 'RAM is fast' to a question asking why RAM is used for currently running programs. Improve this into a full TWO-mark explanation. [2 marks]
st: 'Explain' requires a point and a relevant reason, not only a vague adjective.
RAM stores the instructions and data currently being used by the computer [1].
The CPU can access that working information quickly when executing the running program [1].
Both parts refer to the role of RAM. 'RAM is fast' alone would not secure both marks.

w: A learner needs a durable portable drive. Explain ONE reason an SSD may be preferable to an HDD. [2 marks]
An SSD has no moving parts [1], so it is less likely to be damaged by knocks when carried [1].
Trace this algorithm: total = 2; total = total + 3; print(total). State the total after both assignments and the output. [3 marks]
After first line total=2 [1]; after second line total=5 [1]; the output is 5 [1].
A message claims to be from a bank and demands an immediate password reset through an unfamiliar link. Identify the likely attack and explain one safe response. [3 marks]
Phishing [1]; do not use the link [1] and contact the bank using a known official route to check the request [1].
